memory_update.text: Keep MU as the US-listed HBM reference anchor, but do not let it crowd out smaller toll-road and test-enablement names in later layers.
Promote RMBS to Layer 2 evidence work for HBM interface IP, controller/PHY, and patent-license sensitivity; the key unknown is how directly HBM volume/content converts into revenue.
Promote FORM to Layer 2 evidence work for HBM probe-card exposure; filings and earnings calls already show explicit HBM-linked DRAM probe-card revenue signals.

Need a later pass on non-US or ADR/OTC equipment and inspection names such as Advantest, Teradyne, Camtek, and HBM advanced-packaging metrology suppliers; not included here due to the three-candidate cap and direct US-listed focus.
RMBS should remain in the HBM interface/IP universe as a direct but now larger-cap toll-road candidate; later layers must verify post-PHY-sale economics and actual HBM-linked revenue sensitivity.
FORM is a strong underfollowed HBM test-enablement candidate because probe cards and known-good-die validation sit one step away from obvious HBM makers and AI accelerators.

COHU is a lower-attention HBM inspection/metrology and thermal handler candidate; survival in later layers depends on evidence that the HBM Neon platform and AI datacenter test exposure are revenue-material.

Need a later pass on non-US or OTC-adjacent reference competitors such as Advantest, Tokyo Electron, Disco, Lasertec, SK hynix, Samsung Electronics, Micron, Cadence, Synopsys, and substrate/advanced-packaging suppliers to benchmark US-listed candidates.
RMBS should remain on the HBM interface/IP watchlist despite being above the ideal small/mid-cap band because its HBM controller/interface IP exposure is unusually direct.
FORM is a high-priority underfollowed HBM test-gate candidate: probe cards, wafer-level HBM testing, and HBM-stack/interposer verification fit the Serenity chokepoint lens.
AMKR is a second-order HBM packaging/test infrastructure candidate; evidence is currently less pure than RMBS or FORM and needs validation through customer/program disclosures.

Need a follow-up pass on micro/small-cap speculative shadows such as memory-patent licensors, specialty substrate/interposer suppliers, and HBM validation software vendors; current pass stayed above the USD 300M preference and avoided OTC-heavy litigation names.

The HBM node should be split in later layers into: memory manufacturers, interface/controller IP, wafer/probe test, burn-in/final test, interposer/substrate compatibility, OSAT/advanced packaging, and EDA/validation software.

RMBS should be tracked as an HBM interface/controller IP toll-road candidate rather than as a memory manufacturer; verify materiality through HBM4 IP revenue, royalty renewals, and memory-interface chip growth.

FORM should be tracked as a direct HBM memory-test candidate; key evidence is DRAM probe-card revenue tied to HBM and adoption of high-parallelism/full-wafer contactor technology for HBM4-class testing.

For the HBM interface and memory-stack node, the second-order chokepoints to test in later layers are controller IP, patent-license economics, HBM known-good-die test, probe cards, and advanced packaging process control.

Still need a separate pass for US-listed advanced packaging and metrology names such as ONTO, AMKR, TER, KLAC, and AEHR to decide whether their HBM/AI packaging exposure is direct enough for this node.

node: HBM memory stack, interface IP, and memory-controller ecosystem
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe for the HBM/interface/test node. The clean two-lane map is: Micron as the US-listed reference HBM manufacturer and customer-validation anchor; Rambus as the more direct interface-IP and memory-controller toll-road candidate; FormFactor as the underfollowed HBM probe-card/test-enablement candidate. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Expanded the HBM interface/test ecosystem around three US-listed candidates. The strongest direct fits for this underfollowed pass are Rambus as a memory-interface IP and patent/licensing toll-road, FormFactor as a DRAM/HBM wafer probe and known-good-die enablement supplier, and Cohu as an HBM inspection/metrology and semiconductor test automation supplier. These are not buy/sell recommendations; they are Layer 1B research candidates requiring deeper verification of revenue materiality, customer concentration, competitive positioning, and whether HBM/AI exposure is already priced. Layer 1B expansion for the HBM interface / memory-stack node found three US-listed names with plausible direct or second-order exposure beyond obvious memory manufacturers. The cleanest underfollowed chokepoint candidates are Rambus for HBM / memory-interface IP and FormFactor for HBM wafer/probe-card test enablement. Amkor is included as a larger but still sub-mega-cap packaging/test infrastructure candidate because HBM adoption increases the importance of heterogeneous integration and advanced packaging. Micron, SK hynix, Samsung, NVIDIA, AMD, and TSMC remain reference anchors but are intentionally not
